html:
The Jardwadjali are an Aboriginal Australian people of western Victoria, in the upper Wimmera River country from Gariwerd, the Grampians, west to Lake Bringalbert. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Gariwerd is a range of sandstone ridges that rises out of the plains, and it holds most of the Aboriginal rock art sites in Victoria, with paintings in shelters on its slopes. The Jardwadjali shared these ranges with the Djab Wurrung to the east. Other neighbours on the map include the Gunditjmara and the Wergaia. Squatters arrived soon after Major Thomas Mitchell crossed the area in 1836, and violence over land and sheep followed. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
